h1: Oil Tank Replacement Cost in Newfoundland: What You'll Actually Pay in 2026
heroSub: Real prices for St. John's and the Avalon, in plain Canadian dollars. Most homes land between $3,100 and $3,850 installed, with the old tank gone and a fresh HOST tag on the new one.
introHtml:
Nobody on the Avalon publishes oil tank prices, so most people call around and get a "we'll have to come look" from everyone. That's fair for the tricky jobs, but for a standard outdoor tank swap the numbers don't move much, and you deserve to see them before you pick up the phone. Here's what oil tank replacement costs in Newfoundland in 2026, based on published Atlantic Canada retail pricing, all in CAD.

The short version: a new 200-gallon steel tank installed, with your old tank hauled away, runs about $3,200. A fibreglass or Roth double-wall tank is about $3,850, and a smaller 100-gallon tank for heat-pump backup is around $3,100. Those figures include the HOST inspection and registration, so the tag on your new tank is part of the deal, not a surprise line on the invoice. If you'd rather skip the reading and get a number for your own house, ask for a free written estimate and we'll get it to you quickly.

sections.heading: What moves the price up or down
sections.html:
Every quote starts from the same base: the tank, the labour to swap it, and the HOST inspection. What changes the number is the house itself. These are the things we look at on a site visit, and they're worth thinking about before you call anyone.

  • Tank type and size. A 200-gallon steel tank is the baseline at about $3,200. Fibreglass or Roth double-wall adds roughly $650, and a 100-gallon backup tank comes in a little under steel.
  • Where the old tank sits. An outdoor tank on a stand beside the house is a straightforward pull. A basement tank has to be drained, cut down and carried up the stairs, which is why indoor removals are quoted case by case.
  • Condition of the old tank. A tank that's still sound comes out clean. One that's weeping or has a soft bottom needs more care, and any oil in the ground changes the job entirely.
  • Stand, pad and lines. If the stand is rusted through or the pad has heaved, they get replaced with the tank. Old lines that won't pass inspection get swapped too, and those show up as their own line on the estimate.
  • Access. A tank behind a fence, down a bank or buried in a snowdrift takes longer to get at than one sitting by the driveway.
  • Timing. An expired-tag emergency in the dead of winter may carry an after-hours charge, and that varies by contractor. A planned swap in the fall doesn't.

sections.heading: Steel or fibreglass: what the extra $650 buys you
sections.html:
A steel tank at $3,200 is the cheaper day-one choice, and for a lot of homes it's the right one. Steel is proven, it's what most of the Avalon runs on, and a properly installed one on a solid stand does its job without any drama.

A fibreglass or Roth double-wall tank at $3,850 costs more up front, but it isn't prone to the inside-out rust that finishes off steel tanks, so it carries a longer service life on its HOST tag. If you plan to stay in the house, that usually means one fewer replacement down the road, which more than covers the difference. A fresh tag with plenty of years left on it also reads well to a buyer or an insurer.

If you're weighing the two, our fibreglass upgrade page goes through the trade-offs in more detail. Either way, removal of your old tank and the inspection are built into both prices.

sections.heading: What's in a Harbour Tank Co quote
sections.html:
When we give you a number, it's the number. A replacement quote from us covers the new tank, the labour to set it and hook it up, draining and hauling the old outdoor tank, and the HOST inspection and registration by a licensed inspector. You get the paperwork and the tag, and we deal with the disposal.

What it doesn't cover is anything we can't see from the driveway. If the stand needs replacing, the old tank has leaked into the ground, or the basement stairs won't take a whole tank, we'll tell you on the site visit and put the extra in writing before any work starts. You won't get a bigger bill at the end than the one you agreed to, unless we found something and you approved it first.

We quote the same way whether you're in Mount Pearl, Conception Bay South or out around Bay Roberts. And if all you need is the old tank gone, removal on its own is about $500 for an outdoor domestic tank, with indoor removals quoted after a look.

sections.heading: How to keep the cost down
sections.html:
The cheapest oil tank replacement is the one you plan. Check the expiry date on your HOST tag now, and if it's coming up within the year, book the swap for a mild month. You skip any after-hours rate, you're not scrambling when the truck won't fill you, and you're not heating the house with electric heaters while you wait.

  • Bundle removal with the install. Removal on its own is about $500. Done as part of a replacement, it's already inside the $3,200.
  • Pick the tank for how long you'll be in the house. Selling in a couple of years? Steel is fine. Staying put? The extra $650 for fibreglass is likely cheaper than a second steel swap later on.
  • Ask about the oil that's left. Before anyone quotes you, ask what happens to the fuel still in the old tank so you're not paying for the same oil twice.
  • Get it in writing. A free written estimate from us costs nothing and gives you a real number to compare against, which is more than most contractors on the Avalon will hand you.

If the tag has already expired and the delivery's been refused, don't try to wait it out. Our expired tank emergency line runs 24/7, and getting a tank in fast is almost always cheaper than a week of space heaters and a frozen pipe.

faq.q: How much does oil tank replacement cost in Newfoundland?
faq.a: In 2026, a standard 200-gallon steel tank installed in St. John's or anywhere on the Avalon runs about $3,200, with the old tank removed and the HOST inspection included. A fibreglass or Roth double-wall tank is about $3,850, and a 100-gallon heat-pump backup tank is around $3,100. All prices are in Canadian dollars.

faq.q: Does the price include taking away my old tank?
faq.a: Yes. Our replacement prices include draining, disconnecting and disposing of the old outdoor tank. If the old tank is in the basement, the removal side is quoted case by case, because getting it up the stairs is most of the work.

No. The HOST (Heating Oil Storage Tank) inspection, tag and registration are done by the installer's licensed inspector and are normally part of the install price. You shouldn't be paying a separate inspector to tag a tank you just had installed.

faq.q: What does it cost just to remove an old oil tank?
faq.a: Removal and disposal of an outdoor domestic tank is about $500. Indoor and basement tanks are quoted after a look, since access, doorways and whether the tank has to be cut down all change the job.

faq.q: My tag expired and the oil company won't deliver. Will it cost more?
faq.a: The tank and the install cost the same. What can change is an after-hours or emergency call-out charge, and that varies by contractor, so ask before you book. We run a 24/7 emergency line at (709) 800-3117 and tell you the full number before the truck rolls.
